subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw add core pace-aware autonomous throttling for provider quota windows, and what should the first supported scope be?
rationale: The remaining work defines provider-specific quota semantics, persistence, new config/defaults, status/tool prompt contracts, and autonomous blocking behavior that automation should not invent without maintainer product direction.

options.title: Visibility/context first
options.body: Expose pace context through provider usage, status, and session_status without automatic blocking, then revisit throttling after the data model proves useful.

options.title: Full opt-in throttling
options.body: Design a core policy that persists pace state and gates subagents or non-interactive work only behind explicit upgrade-safe config.

options.title: Plugin/API primitives only
options.body: Keep Anthropic-specific pacing policy outside core and add only the generic provider usage or admission hooks that plugins cannot currently express.

recommendation.title: Visibility/context first
recommendation.body: Expose pace context through provider usage, status, and session_status without automatic blocking, then revisit throttling after the data model proves useful.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent current-main history for provider usage/status behavior and adjacent product-scope changes.
